ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the suspended straight rod $AB$ has length $a$. Below point $B$ at a distance $h$, there is a bottomless cylindrical tube $CD$ of length $b$. If the suspension wire is cut, 1. What is the time for the lower end $B$ of the straight rod to pass through the cylinder?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the provided figure, it can be seen that the upper part is a fixed supporting surface, and a vertical suspension string is hanging a vertical straight rod. The vicinity of the upper end of the rod is marked as A, the lower end is marked as B, and on the left side a double-headed arrow marks the rod length a. The given image screenshot does not clearly show the lower cylinder CD; combined with the problem statement, the upper opening of the cylinder is at a distance h below point B, and the length of the cylinder is b. Reasoning: After the suspension string is cut, the straight rod as a whole starts to fall freely from rest, and the lower end B of the rod, together with the rod, makes vertical falling motion with initial velocity 0 and acceleration g. When B reaches the upper opening of the cylinder, the falling distance is h, so from s=\tfrac12 gt^2, t_1=\sqrt{2h/g}. When B passes through and leaves the lower opening of the cylinder, the falling distance is h+b, therefore t_2=\sqrt{2(h+b)/g}. Therefore the time used for end B to pass through the cylinder is the difference between the two moments: \Delta t=t_2-t_1=\sqrt{\frac{2(h+b)}{g}}-\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}.
